claims.statement: Every OpenWiki connector implements the ConnectorRuntime contract: a static ConnectorDefinition (id, displayName, description, backend, mode, requiredEnv, supportsAgenticDiscovery) plus an ingest() method returning a ConnectorIngestResult with status success/skipped/error, runId, rawFiles, statePath, message, and warnings.

ConnectorId is a closed union of nine connector ids (custom-mcp, git-repo, google, hackernews, langsmith, notion, slack, web-search, x) and ConnectorBackend is one of direct-api, local-git, mcp-http, or mcp-stdio.

createConnectorRegistry() builds a fresh map from every ConnectorId to its runtime, wiring custom-mcp and notion through createMcpConnector and the remaining connectors through their per-source factory functions; CONNECTOR_IDS is the canonical id enumeration.

getConfiguredConnectorIds() returns connector ids that require auth and have all required env vars set, used only as a telemetry adoption signal, and isConnectorId() validates arbitrary strings against the ConnectorId union.

Connectors persist under ~/.openwiki/connectors/<id>/ with config in config.json (merged over a default, missing file falls back to the default), state in state.json, and raw dumps in raw/<run-id>/<file>.json where the run id is an ISO timestamp with ':' and '.' replaced by '-'.
Connector state is versioned (version:1) and updateStateWithRun prepends each run summary to the runs history and truncates it to the 20 most recent runs while recording lastRunAt.
Connector state and raw files are written with owner-only permissions (files 0600, directories 0700) via writePrivateJson.

Connector ids are validated with assertSafeConnectorId and raw reads/writes are confined inside the connector's raw/ directory: resolveConnectorRawPath rejects any relative path that resolves outside raw/, preventing path traversal outside the staging area.

createOpenWikiConnectorTools returns an empty tool array for repository (code) output mode, so codebase-documentation runs are never handed connector ingestion tools; the connector tools are wired into the agent from this factory.

In personal/local-wiki mode the connector tool set exposes openwiki_list_connectors, openwiki_list_mcp_tools, openwiki_call_mcp_tool, openwiki_ingest_connector, openwiki_ingest_all_connectors, openwiki_list_raw_items, and openwiki_read_raw_item; each runs through reportToolResult, which returns a failure to the model as an {error} JSON result instead of throwing so a failed tool does not end the agent run.
The MCP discovery/call tools accept only custom-mcp and notion as connectorId; openwiki_list_mcp_tools and openwiki_call_mcp_tool reject any non-MCP-backed connector.

listConnectors and the raw-read tools never return secret values: required env vars are reported as presence-only status, and readRawItem caps a read at 500 KB, confines it to the connector raw directory, refuses symbolic links and non-files with RawItemAccessError.
createMcpConnector builds both custom-mcp and notion from one shared runtime whose backend is mcp-stdio, mode personal, and supportsAgenticDiscovery true.

MCP connector ingest is enable/config gated: not enabled returns skipped, missing transport or readOnlyOperations returns error, an empty readOnlyOperations list lists MCP tools and returns skipped without guessing, and a populated list executes the read-only operations and returns success.
MCP connector config resolution uses on-disk config.json as the base and lets an ingest-time connectorConfig override win field-by-field without inventing defaults.

getToolCallPolicy enforces read-only MCP tool calls: a tool is allowed only if listed in connector config allowedTools, or annotated readOnlyHint:true, or (for notion only) served by the hosted https://mcp.notion.com/mcp endpoint with a read-only-looking name/description; otherwise it is rejected.

callMcpConnectorTool rejects any tool name not returned by a live tools/list discovery with McpToolCallRefusedError (reason unknown_tool), forcing agents to discover and use exact tool names before calling; a tool the read-only policy refuses raises the same error with reason not_read_only.
Persisted MCP transports are sanitized before being written into raw dumps: sanitizeMcpTransport replaces ${ENV} references in headers with <env-ref> so secret env references never land in raw files.
The MCP client speaks JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio (a spawned child process with shell:false) or HTTP, dispatching read-only operations, tool calls, and tools/list to the matching transport.

HTTP MCP URLs must use https except for http to localhost, and HTTP MCP headers must reference credentials as ${ENV_VAR} (never a literal secret); env references resolve from process.env or, for OAuth access-token env keys, through the OAuth token layer. resolveEnvReference treats an env var explicitly set to an empty string ("") as present, not missing — only a truly undefined variable (typeof undefined) throws the 'required for MCP connector ingestion' error, mirroring buildChildEnv's typeof value === "string" check for base env vars.
MCP tools/list is fully paginated but bounded twice against a misbehaving server: iteration stops on a repeated cursor and on a 100-page cap.

MCP stdio commands and args are validated (command pattern allowlist, no control characters in args), and each JSON-RPC request times out after 60s with the child killed on close, so a hung server cannot block ingestion.

The git-repo connector is a local-git backend with no required env and supportsAgenticDiscovery false that reads configured local clones and writes compact per-repo manifests (branch, HEAD, recent commits, status, changed files), records each repo's HEAD as a latestIds cursor, skips repos with unsafe ids, and is incremental: createRepoManifest resolves a usable previous head via resolveReachableHead (verifying the recorded commit is still reachable with git rev-parse --verify before diffing against it), and when previousHead is undefined, matches the current head, or is no longer reachable (history rewritten/force-push), falls back to the working-tree diff (git diff --name-status HEAD) rather than failing.

The Gmail connector (id google) is a direct-api backend that fetches recent Gmail messages via the Gmail API and requires OAuth access and refresh token env vars (OPENWIKI_GMAIL_ACCESS_TOKEN and OPENWIKI_GMAIL_REFRESH_TOKEN).

The Slack connector is a direct-api backend requiring OPENWIKI_SLACK_USER_TOKEN that fetches conversations, recent messages, and assistant search context across recent_messages, my_messages_search, and assistant_search streams.
The X/Twitter connector is a direct-api backend requiring OPENWIKI_X_ACCESS_TOKEN that fetches home timeline, user posts, mentions, list posts, and bookmarks via X API v2 with OAuth user context.

The web-search connector is a direct-api backend requiring TAVILY_API_KEY that runs Tavily searches via the LangChain Tavily integration; it is enabled by default but produces nothing without configured queries.
The Hacker News connector is a direct-api backend with no required env that pulls public HN feeds (Firebase) and Algolia search results without credentials.

The LangSmith connector is the only code-mode connector: it requires a repoRoot and committed repo workspace config, requires OPENWIKI_LANGSMITH_API_KEY (with additional per-workspace key env vars), and skips cleanly when invoked without a repoRoot or configured workspaces.

The LangSmith connector pulls an anomaly-weighted trace sample capped at 20 traces (errors first up to 10, then latency outliers up to 5) and degrades per-workspace/per-project failures to warnings rather than failing the whole run.

All direct-API connectors and the HTTP MCP client fetch through fetchWithResilience, which adds a per-attempt timeout and bounded exponential backoff with full jitter on 429/5xx and network errors (honoring Retry-After within a cap) while returning 401/403 and other 4xx unchanged so callers can refresh tokens instead of retrying.

Adding a connector requires registering its id in types.ts and registry.ts and implementing a ConnectorRuntime under src/connectors/sources/, but the documented preference is to reuse custom-mcp for any read-only MCP server and add a bespoke connector only for provider-specific auth, scoping, or deterministic pulls MCP cannot express.

Connector authoring rules require secrets to live in ~/.openwiki/.env referenced only by env var name (never read, logged, returned, or hardcoded), connector ids and raw paths to be validated, incremental sources to store cursors/hashes, and any wrapped MCP server to be treated as read-only.

The X connector isolates per-stream failures: each stream (and each list within list_posts) is fetched independently, and a failure on one stream (e.g. a 429 on mentions) records a warning and moves on rather than aborting the whole run — already-fetched dumps are kept, other streams keep going, and state is still written so successful streams' since_id cursors advance.

The X connector's run status is success when at least one dump was produced, error when nothing was fetched but a stream failed (not a benign skipped), and skipped when there was no configured work to do.

ingestAllConnectors runs every connector concurrently with Promise.allSettled and isolates per-connector failures: one connector that throws does not discard the results of connectors that succeeded, and each rejection is converted to an error result via ingestFailureResult so the agent still sees every outcome.
Only the MCP-backed connectors (custom-mcp, notion) set supportsAgenticDiscovery true; ingestion accepts an injected connectorRegistry so callers can replay recorded pulls instead of fetching.
